page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 31.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB per core. For hardware acceleration, it includes a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included, requiring external block storage, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance split between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The Intel Xeon 8163 CPU demonstrates weak performance in general-purpose compute benchmarks, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Similarly, memory bandwidth and database operations show weak to average performance. However, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong results in machine learning tasks. LLM inference speed for prompt processing is in the top 10% for both small (135M) and medium (7B) models, while text generation for the 7B model ranks in the top 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance serves as an entry-level GPU platform. It trades off high-performance CPU capabilities and local storage for affordable access to hardware acceleration. This resource profile makes the instance highly suitable for lightweight deep learning inference, small-to-medium LLM deployment, and basic video transcoding, rather than heavy general-purpose compute or high-throughput database hosting.

Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance lacks local storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. While CPU-bound benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the processor in the bottom 25%, the integrated Turing-architecture GPU excels at machine learning tasks. Notably, LLM inference for prompt processing ranks in the top 10% for both 135M and 7B models. This instance offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads, making it highly suitable for lightweight AI inference, model deployment, and parallel computing tasks where CPU performance is not the primary bottleneck.
